analysis:
The PR changes one documentation row in docs/architecture/inference.md (line 1846, outside the supplied excerpts; the patch is visible in file_changes). It describes the `stop` parameter: matching stays on held-back detokenised text (StopHoldback), and GPT-OSS now sets `stopStringScope` to the Harmony `final` message via `ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope`, so analysis and tool-call frames never match. The reported stop sequence replays the same scope. The two supplied units are unchanged surrounding base text (lines 2429-2954) covering MiMo, Flint, Qwen4 and invariants. They show no changes of their own.

Security relevance: this is documentation only. It describes a behavioral scope narrowing for stop strings on GPT-OSS, with no new endpoints, trust boundaries, key handling, attestation, cache storage or authorization. The T-041 prefix cache, SSD tier, TTL and HMAC naming are untouched. I found no regression or invalidated threat assumption.

Unverified contract: the actual code change in ModelEOSPolicy, StopHoldback and EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift is not supplied. I cannot confirm that the described scoping fails closed, for example that analysis text or tool-call frames cannot leak through stop matching. I also cannot confirm that the reported stop sequence cannot reveal hidden reasoning content. Source review of those files should check that the scope replay does not expose withheld analysis channel text to the consumer. That concern is hypothetical and not a finding. The doc statement is plausibly an improvement, since it prevents analysis text from truncating output.
